entries.test: Whether leading AI labs' models stay at near-parity on major benchmarks and whether any lab keeps a durable market-share or pricing premium.
entries.note: He asserts the premise outright, so it should not be listed as a condition. 'Moat' is loose, but the plain reading is that no lab has a durable competitive advantage.

entries.test: Whether frontier-model API and subscription prices show competitive price cuts and converge toward commodity levels instead of holding monopoly-level margins.
entries.note: This is written as general economic reasoning in the present tense. Current pricing data can already test it.

entries.test: Whether AI companies' eventual profits fall well short of the capital and valuations invested in them, shown by write-downs, low returns on AI capex, or valuations collapsing.
entries.note: 'Everybody' means the firms and investors betting on a winner-take-all outcome. The forecast has no deadline.
Both halves are vague: 'the economics don't make sense' and 'more and more people are starting to notice'. He explicitly makes no prediction about when a collapse would come.
